description: Witness statements used to test the statement parser on layouts other than Rod Ismay's. Chosen by surveying all 131 statements in data/raw/statements/ (excluding WITN0463*, Ismay's) for variety: text layer quality, numbering style, sub-paragraphs, headings, length and solicitors. Every PDF in the collection has a text layer (each page is a scan with OCR underneath), so the 'scanned' picks are the ones whose text layer is garbled. Paths are relative to statements_dir.

statements.why: Pages 12, 13, 17 and 18 have a garbled text layer (page 13: 11% word-like tokens); re-running OCR recovers whole paragraphs (40-43). Also lettered/roman lists.

statements.file: WITN05290200 - David Smith - Second Witness Statement.pdf
statements.why: Poor scan: body text on page 16 is garbled in the text layer ('I ~eppuntd wt ih...'), and the statement of truth reads 'StateTent of Tnnth'.
Mostly sub-paragraphs, up to three levels (2.6.1, 19.4.1), with OCR damage in the numbers ('26.3' for 2.6.3).
Sub-paragraphs written '6.1.' with a trailing full stop; OCR reads 'I' as '1' ('5. 1 have'). Prepared with Kingsley Napley.
Many lettered list items and headings; wrapped lines that start with a number ('4 in assessing'). DAC Beachcroft LLP.
Heaviest use of headings in the collection, a Part structure, and (a)/(b) lists within paragraphs. Manches LLP.
Longest statement; paragraphs numbered without a full stop ('4 I have addressed...').
Headings and sub-paragraphs; OCR reads '11. I also' as '11.1 also', which looks like a sub-paragraph. Ashfords LLP.

statements.file: WITN03510100 Sir Geoffrey Mulgan - Witness staement.pdf
statements.why: Short; OCR artefacts '11.1 had' (for '11. I had') and '| had' (for 'I had').
Short with many paragraphs (about 30); OCR artefacts '11. 1 would', 'Dueto', 'Iwas'.
